'''Bartolomeo Sovero''' (1576{{snd}}23 July 1629) was a Swiss [[mathematician]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.uriland.it/matematica/BBB.html|title=  Bullettino di Bibliografia e Storia delle Scienze Matematiche e Fisiche}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Sovero was born in Corbières in 1576. In 1594 he entered the Jesuit order and studied logic, mathematics and theology at the Jesuit College of Brera. In 1604 he left the Society of Jesus.{{sfn|Nenci|2019}} in 1624 Sovero replaced [[Giovanni Camillo Glorioso]] on the chair of mathematics at the [[University of Padua]].{{sfn|Nenci|2019}} In his main work, ''Curvi ac recti proportio'', Sovero proves to be a precursor of the [[Method of Indivisibles|geometry of indivisibles]] and of the method called "proportional parallel movement". It is elucidated by an algebraic formulation. The work of Sovero gave rise to two important polemics, one with the first successor of [[Galileo Galilei|Galileo]] in Padua, [[Giovanni Camillo Glorioso|Glorioso]]; the second between [[Paul Guldin|Guldin]] and [[Bonaventura Cavalieri|Cavalieri]] on the subject of the latter's originality.
